## Opportunities at North-West University

**Closing date: 25 October 2026**

The School of Mathematical and Statistical Sciences in the Faculty of Natural and Agricultural Sciences at North-West University (Potchefstroom Campus) is recruiting for the following post.

### Associate Professor in Statistics (V002765)

[Download the full advert (PDF)](files/jobs/NWU-Associate-Professor-in-Statistics-V002765.pdf)

**Peromnes grade:** A4
**Employment type:** Permanent appointment
**Planned commencement of duties:** As soon as possible

#### Purpose of the position

An experienced academic in mathematical statistics. The candidate must have ample experience in teaching and learning, successfully completing research projects, including publications in national and international accredited scientific journals. The candidate will be expected to act as mentor of junior staff in the department. The candidate will be responsible for lecturing undergraduate and postgraduate statistics modules and can also be expected to be involved in the development of new modules. Other duties include the supervision or co-supervision of PhD and master's student projects.

#### Minimum requirements

- A PhD (NQF Level 10) in Mathematical Statistics.
- A minimum of five (5) years' experience working with the administration of large class groups.
- A minimum of five (5) years' experience in teaching undergraduate and postgraduate mathematical statistics courses.
- A proven publication track record of a minimum of five (5) articles.
- A proven track record of supervising students at a PhD and Master's level.

#### Key functional and technical competencies

The candidate must be able to:

- Present both undergraduate and postgraduate statistics modules.
- Act as a group coordinator for modules with multiple groups.
- Handle large undergraduate classes.
- Supervise honours students.
- Communicate well in English (verbally and in writing).
- Analyse data using advanced statistical techniques by means of suitable statistical computer packages (such as SAS, R, SPSS and STATISTICA).
- Provide guidance with regards to data collection and data analysis.

#### Key behavioural competencies

- Professional and ethical behaviour.
- Work well independently and within a team.
- Have very good people skills.
- Be able to act as a mentor for junior staff.

#### Key responsibilities

- **Teaching and learning:** Presenting undergraduate and postgraduate statistics modules. Development of new modules and programmes.
- **Research:** Conducting academic research (publishing of research papers, etc.) and supervision of postgraduate (PhD and Master's) students.
- **Administration and management:** Help with administrative, organisational and management tasks within the subject group.

#### Added advantages

- Membership with the South African Statistical Association.

**Remuneration:** The annual total remuneration package will be commensurate with the level of appointment as advertised and in line with the NWU policy guidelines.

**Enquiries regarding job content:** Prof David Kubayi, Tel 018 299 2669

**Enquiries regarding the recruitment process:** Dolly Lebepe, Tel 018 285 2037

### How to apply

Applications must be submitted online through the official NWU vacancy website. Incomplete applications and those submitted through any other platform will not be considered.

- The University subscribes to and applies the principles of the Employment Equity (EE) Act and is committed to transformation. Preference will be given to candidates from the designated groups, in accordance with the principles of the EE Act and the NWU Employment Equity Plan.
- The University reserves the right not to make an appointment. Communication will be limited to shortlisted candidates only.
- If you are not contacted within two months from the closing date of this advertisement, please accept that your application was unsuccessful.

## Opportunities at the University of Limpopo

**Closing date: 23 October 2026**

The Department of Statistics and Operation Research in the Faculty of Science and Agriculture at the University of Limpopo is recruiting for the following posts.

### Professor (Statistics)

[Download the full advert (PDF)](files/jobs/Professor-Department-of-Statistics-and-Operation-Research.pdf)

#### Qualifications and requirements

- PhD in the field of Statistics.
- At least ten (10) years of relevant research and teaching experience at tertiary level.
- Appropriate administrative experience.
- Supervised at least two (2) PhD students to completion in the relevant discipline.
- Evidence of publication in DHET accredited journals, that is, at least ten (10) publications.
- Evidence of good publication track record, including recent publications.
- Record of lecturing Statistics modules at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
- Ability and evidence of sourcing third-stream income.
- Evidence of the ability to establish collaborations and raise research funds.
- Experience and expertise in the use of various statistical software packages such as SAS, R, Python, SPSS, STATA, etc.
- Evidence of community engagement activities.

#### Duties and responsibilities

- Teach students at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
- Supervise postgraduate students at all levels (Honours, Masters, PhD).
- Conduct research in any of the branches of Statistics.
- Engage in community outreach programmes.
- Contribute to departmental, school and faculty administration as required.
- Contribute to curriculum development.

#### Added advantages

- NRF rating.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Excellent research and postgraduate supervision record.
- Evidence of proposal writing skills for funding purposes.
- Evidence of participation in academic administration.
- Evidence of academic leadership.

**Enquiries regarding conditions of service:** Ms BT Tshehla, Tel 015 268 3513

**Employment equity preference:** African males and African females.

### Professor / Associate Professor (Operations Research)

[Download the full advert (PDF)](files/jobs/Professor-Associate-Professor-Department-of-Statistics-and-Operation-Research.pdf)

#### Qualifications and requirements

- Record of lecturing Operations Research courses/modules at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
- Ability and evidence of sourcing third-stream income.
- Evidence of the ability to establish collaborations and raise research funds.
- Experience and expertise in the use of various statistical software packages such as SAS, R, Python, SPSS, STATA, etc.
- Evidence of community engagement activities.

#### Duties and responsibilities

- Teach students at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels.
- Teach the Operational Research modules for undergraduate levels and develop a postgraduate curriculum.
- Supervise postgraduate students at all levels (Honours, Masters, PhD).
- Conduct research in any of the branches of Operations Research or Statistics.
- Engage in community outreach programmes.
- Contribute to departmental, school and faculty administration as required.

#### Added advantages

- NRF rating.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.
- Proven research record and teaching in Operations Research.
- Evidence of proposal writing skills for funding purposes.
- Evidence of participation in academic administration.
- Evidence of academic leadership for Professorship level.

**Enquiries regarding conditions of service:** Ms BT Tshehla, Tel 015 268 3740

**Employment equity preference:** Professor: African males and African females. Associate Professor: African and Indian males, and African females.

[Download the full advert (PDF)](files/jobs/Senior-Lecturer-Department-of-Statistics-and-Operation-Research.pdf)

**Enquiries regarding conditions of service:** Ms BT Tshehla, Tel 015 268 3740

### How to apply

Please submit a cover letter clearly indicating which post you are applying for, a detailed CV with all your names, addresses, contact details and e-mail address, and the contact numbers of three (3) referees. Include certified copies of all qualifications, including your Matric / Grade 12 certificate, academic transcripts, and a South African ID or passport. E-mail applications to the Human Resources Officer at [recruitment9@ul.ac.za](mailto:recruitment9@ul.ac.za).

- It is the applicant's responsibility to have foreign qualifications evaluated by the South African Qualifications Authority (SAQA).
- Failure to submit the requested documents or information will result in your application not being considered.
- The University of Limpopo is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All appointments will be made in accordance with the University's Employment Equity Policy.
- Correspondence will be limited to short-listed candidates only. Applicants who have not been contacted within 30 days of the closing date must consider their applications unsuccessful.
- The University reserves the right not to make an appointment.
